title: Network isolation: private endpoints, egress control, and the subnet that reached the internet

videos.script: A subnet called private is not private because of its name. {{title}} It is private because of its routes. If its route table sends everything to an internet gateway, it is public. {{table}} And a subnet with no table of its own follows the main table of its network. {{main}} So one route, added to the main table for a test machine, can reach the patient records database. Nobody touched the database. {{caio}} This lesson builds the clinic's network in your lab, makes that mistake, and takes it back. {{fix}} Then it looks the other way, at what leaves. Every new security group lets everything out. {{egress}} You will close that, and give the database a private path to its backups, through an endpoint. {{endpoint}} Then you write a short program that asks every subnet where it leads. {{checker}} And you will see what flow logs record, and what they never will. {{end}}
